name: Screen size and density
plain: Reads pixel size, density and scale factor with no prompt.
meaning: Identifies the device model almost uniquely on iPhone and narrows it on Android. Needed for layout; also a long-lived fingerprint field.

android.note: Density 120 to 640 dpi; size in px

ios.api_surface: Scale 2.0 or 3.0 on iPhone; bounds in points

limits.headline: Can see your screen size, sharpness and scale, with no prompt
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app checks when it opens, to lay out its screens
can: See screen width and height, in pixels on Android and points on iPhone
See sharpness, 120 to 640 dpi on Android and scale 2 or 3 on iPhone
Fit its layout to your screen
See window size on newer Android
cannot: Learn who you are from screen size alone
See what is on screen in other apps

story.what_it_is: An app can read the size of your screen and how sharp it is.
story.for_you: You never see it. It is needed to draw the app properly. It also tells an app almost exactly which phone you have.
story.for_makers: Makers need it to lay out screens for every size. Because the numbers are so specific, they also work as a long lasting fingerprint detail.

use_cases.example: A game scales its menus and touch buttons to fit your exact screen.
A store app shows a grid with two or three product columns depending on your width.
A drawing app sizes its canvas to the screen sharpness.
A video app picks a video size that fits your screen and saves data.
An ad network picks an ad size and joins it with other details to guess your phone.
A reading app lets you pick larger text based on your screen density.

story.android_note: Reads pixel size, density and scale factor with no prompt.
story.ios_note: Reads size and scale, which pins down the iPhone model.

technical_bounds: Multi-window and foldables report window, not screen, size

refs.label: Kurtz et al.: Fingerprinting Mobile Devices Using Personalized Configurations (PoPETs 2016)
